x: Chas. however, must have produced the fastest last 880 of the race in his effort to make every place count. In the finishing straight a floundering Ken Harland ( Cambridge H.) was all but knocked over by Charlie's slip-stream!

In those early halcyon days he beat most of his contempories - names like George Knight, Peter Driver, Ken Harland, Eddie Ellis, Jack Heywood and Ian Boyd - and, no doubt, he is tempted at times to think of what might have been.
Lionel Mann held 3rd place on Stage two by displacing Woodford but had to give way to an evergreen Ken Harland who took Cambridge H. from 5th to 2nd.
Cambridge H had taken the lead with a fine run from veteran Ken Harland, while young Dave Clarke of Hercules Wimbledon set the day's fastest short lap time of 15:40.

Two days later, the day after his 45th birthday, Laurie went for the group 1B 5,000 metres and came away with another win in 15:21.4 - a pretty shrewd move because Ken Harland of Cambridge H took the 1A event in 14:56.4.
